examples.ko: 새로 산 김치냉장고에 김치를 가득 넣었어요.
examples.en: I filled the new kimchi refrigerator with kimchi.

examples.ko: 우리 집은 김치냉장고가 두 대 있어요.
examples.en: My family has two kimchi refrigerators.

examples.ko: 김치냉장고 덕분에 김치를 오래 두고 먹어요.
examples.en: Thanks to the kimchi refrigerator, I can keep kimchi for a long time.
My mother brought some kimchi out of the kimchi refrigerator.
I'm going to put the kimchi refrigerator in the corner of the kitchen.
When we move, shall we take the kimchi refrigerator too?

explain: 일반 냉장고와 따로 두고 쓰는, 김치를 보관하는 전용 냉장고예요. 그래서 '냉장고'와 구별해서 말하고, 물건은 한 대, 두 대로 세요.
explain_en: This is a separate refrigerator used only for storing kimchi, so people distinguish it from a regular '냉장고'. You count it with 대: 한 대, 두 대.

examples.en: Seolleongtang has to come with kkakdugi.
Kkakdugi is made by cutting radish into cubes.

examples.ko: 깍두기 국물이 너무 맛있어서 밥을 비볐어요.
examples.en: The kkakdugi juice was so good that I mixed it into my rice.
I want to eat doenjang stew with kimchi and kkakdugi.

examples.ko: 어머니가 담근 깍두기를 조금 나눠 주셨어요.
examples.en: My mother shared some of the kkakdugi she made.

examples.ko: 이 깍두기는 너무 시어서 못 먹겠어요.
examples.en: This kkakdugi is too sour for me to eat.

explain: 배추김치와 달리 무로 만든 김치예요. 설렁탕, 곰탕, 국밥 같은 국물 음식과 같이 나올 때가 많아요. '깍두기'는 모양 때문에 네모나게 썬 것을 가리키기도 해요.

phrases.example: 사람이 모자라서 막내는 깍두기로 끼워 줬어요.
phrases.en: We were short on players, so we let the youngest join in as a 'kkakdugi'.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아이들 놀이에서 나이가 어리거나 실력이 모자라서 어느 편에도 속하지 않고 양쪽에 끼는 사람을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: In children's games, it refers to a player who is too young or less skilled and joins in without belonging to a fixed team.

explain_en: Unlike cabbage kimchi, this kimchi is made from radish. It often comes with soup dishes such as seolleongtang, gomtang and gukbap. The word can also describe things cut into small cubes.

examples.en: The new pencil was sharpened to a very fine point.
The rock was worn down by the waves, so it is round.
I bought it at the market for a heavily discounted price.
The skin of this potato peels easily.

examples.ko: 칼이 무뎌서 연필이 잘 깎이지 않아요.
examples.en: The knife is dull, so the pencil doesn't get sharpened well.
I'm worried that my score will be docked if I'm late.

explain: '깎다'의 피동이라서 연필, 과일, 바위처럼 깎는 대상이 주어가 돼요. 값이나 월급, 점수가 줄어들 때도 써요. '값을 깎아 주다'는 사람이 하는 행동이고, '값이 깎이다'는 그 결과예요.
explain_en: This is the passive of '깎다', so the thing being cut, like a pencil, fruit or rock, is the subject. It is also used when a price, salary or score is reduced. '값을 깎아 주다' is the person's action, while '값이 깎이다' is the result.

examples.en: It's delicious to wrap meat in a perilla leaf and eat it.
I like perilla leaves because their scent is strong.
We grow perilla leaves on our balcony.
What did you plant in the garden? Chili peppers and perilla.
I ate rice topped with pickled perilla leaves.
I bought a bunch of perilla leaves at the market.

explain: 영어로 sesame leaf라고 옮기지만 실제로는 들깨의 잎이에요. 쌈, 장아찌, 전, 김치로 먹고 향이 강해서 좋아하는 사람과 싫어하는 사람이 나뉘어요. 발음은 [깬닙]이에요.
explain_en: It is often translated as 'sesame leaf', but it is actually the leaf of the perilla plant (들깨). It is eaten as a wrap, pickle, in pancakes and as kimchi, and its strong scent divides people. The pronunciation is [깬닙].

examples.en: If you memorize the times tables, division gets easy too.
I solved ten division problems.
My child is good at addition but finds division hard.
In division, there is sometimes a remainder.
Doing division on a calculator is fast.
Teacher, what's the answer to this division problem?

explain: 덧셈, 뺄셈, 곱셈, 나눗셈이 사칙연산 짝이에요. 식을 읽을 때는 '육 나누기 이는 삼'처럼 '나누기'를 써요. '나눗셈'은 사이시옷이 있어서 '나누셈'이 아니라 '나눗셈'으로 써요.
explain_en: It belongs with 덧셈, 뺄셈 and 곱셈 as the four arithmetic operations. When you read an equation aloud, you say '육 나누기 이는 삼' with '나누기'. Spell it with the ㅅ: 나눗셈, not 나누셈.

examples.en: The delivery food came with wooden chopsticks.
Split the wooden chopsticks in half and use them.
You use wooden chopsticks once and throw them away.
For lunch I ate cup noodles with wooden chopsticks and enjoyed it.
Please give me two more pairs of wooden chopsticks.
A splinter from the wooden chopsticks got stuck in my hand.

explain: 한 번 쓰고 버리는 일회용 젓가락이에요. 보통 붙어 있는 걸 반으로 쪼개서 써요. 세는 말은 '벌'이고, 금속 젓가락은 '쇠젓가락'이라고 해요.
explain_en: These are disposable chopsticks, usually joined together so that you split them apart before use. You count them with 벌, and metal chopsticks are called '쇠젓가락'.

examples.en: My friend is coming to Korea the day after tomorrow.
I haven't studied, and the exam is the day after tomorrow.
Then I'll contact you again around the day after tomorrow.

examples.ko: 오늘은 바빠서 내일모레 만날 수 있어요.
examples.en: I'm busy today, so I can meet the day after tomorrow.
Vacation starts the day after tomorrow, so I'm going on a trip.

examples.ko: 내일모레 여행 가는데 짐을 아직 못 쌌어요.
examples.en: I'm leaving on a trip the day after tomorrow, but I haven't packed yet.

explain: '모레'와 같은 뜻으로 쓰고, 멀지 않은 가까운 앞날을 가리키기도 해요. 그래서 날짜를 정확히 말할 때는 '모레'가 더 분명해요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 나이에 곧 닿는다는 뜻으로, 나이를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when talking about age, meaning someone will reach that age very soon.

explain_en: It means the same as '모레' and can also point to the near future in general. If you want to name the exact day clearly, '모레' is more precise.

examples.en: It was hot, so I ordered an iced coffee.
Please put lots of ice in my iced coffee.
I like iced coffee better than hot coffee.
Iced coffee tastes watery when the ice melts.
In summer I make iced coffee at home and drink it.
Two iced coffees to go, please.

explain: '냉'은 차갑다는 뜻이고 반대는 '따뜻한 커피'예요. 카페에서는 '아이스커피'나 '아이스 아메리카노'처럼 말하는 사람도 많아요.
explain_en: The '냉' part means cold, and the opposite is '따뜻한 커피' (hot coffee). In cafés many people say '아이스커피' or '아이스 아메리카노' instead.

examples.en: When the yellow light comes on, I slow down.
The traffic light turned yellow while I was crossing.
It's dangerous to just drive through when the light is yellow.
Don't rush across when the light is yellow.
The car in front suddenly stopped at the yellow light.
There's a traffic light where only the yellow keeps blinking.

explain: 신호등은 빨간불, 노란불, 초록불 순서로 말해요. 초록불은 '파란불'이라고 부르는 사람도 많아요. 노란불에는 멈출 준비를 하라는 신호예요.
explain_en: Traffic lights are named 빨간불, 노란불 and 초록불. Many people call the green light '파란불' too. The yellow light is a signal to get ready to stop.

examples.en: The ginkgo leaves turned yellow as autumn colors came in.

examples.ko: 큰 소리에 갑자기 놀라서 얼굴이 노래졌어요.
examples.en: I was startled by the loud noise and my face went pale.

examples.ko: 오래 둔 종이는 시간이 지나면 노래져요.
examples.en: Paper left for a long time turns yellow as time passes.

examples.ko: 카레 국물이 튀어서 옷이 노래져 버렸어요.
examples.en: Curry splashed on my clothes and turned them yellow.
You can eat a banana once the peel turns yellow.
They harvest the rice around the time it turns yellow.

explain: '노랗다'에 '-아지다'가 붙은 말이고, ㅎ 불규칙이라서 '노래요, 노래져요'가 돼요. '노랗게 되다'라고 풀어 말할 수도 있어요. 반대로 하얗게 되면 '하얘지다'라고 해요.
explain_en: This is '노랗다' plus '-아지다', and since it is a ㅎ-irregular adjective it becomes '노래요, 노래져요'. You can also say '노랗게 되다'. The parallel for white is '하얘지다'.

examples.en: I can hear the children singing in the classroom.
Cheerful singing can be heard from somewhere too.
I couldn't sleep because of the singing.
I woke up to the singing from next door.
That singer's voice is really clear.

examples.ko: 노랫소리를 따라가 보니 작은 공원이 나왔어요.
examples.en: I followed the sound of singing and came to a small park.

explain: '노래'와 '소리'가 합쳐지면서 사이시옷이 들어가서 '노래소리'가 아니라 '노랫소리'라고 써요. '목소리'는 사람의 목소리 자체이고, '노랫소리'는 노래하는 소리예요.
explain_en: When '노래' and '소리' join, a 사이시옷 is added, so write '노랫소리', not '노래소리'. '목소리' is a person's voice itself, while '노랫소리' is the sound of singing.

examples.en: I fell and cracked my leg bone.

examples.ko: 다리뼈가 부러져서 한 달 동안 깁스했어요.
examples.en: I broke my leg bone and wore a cast for a month.
I had my leg bone X-rayed.
The child's leg bones are still growing.
There is a fossil of a dinosaur leg bone in the museum.
The length of leg bones differs slightly from person to person.

explain: 다리에 있는 뼈를 통틀어 부르는 말이에요. 병원에서 구체적으로 말할 때는 '정강이뼈'처럼 부위 이름을 쓰기도 해요. 뼈가 '부러지다', '금이 가다'와 자주 같이 써요.
explain_en: It is a general word for the bones of the leg. At a hospital people may use specific names such as '정강이뼈' (shinbone). It often goes with '부러지다' (break) and '금이 가다' (crack).

examples.ko: 아침에 보니 창문이 깨끗하게 닦여 있어요.
examples.en: This morning I saw that the windows had been wiped clean.

examples.ko: 이 얼룩은 아무리 문질러도 안 닦여요.
examples.en: This stain won't come off no matter how much I rub it.
After mopping, the floor was wiped clean and shiny.

examples.ko: 이 천은 먼지가 잘 닦이는 것 같아요.
examples.en: This cloth seems to wipe dust off well.

examples.ko: 아직 닦이지 않은 접시가 하나 남았어요.
examples.en: There is one plate left that hasn't been wiped yet.

examples.ko: 말끔히 닦인 신발을 보니 기분이 좋아요.
examples.en: I feel good seeing the shoes wiped spotless.

explain: '닦다'의 피동이라서 닦는 사람보다 닦이는 물건과 그 상태를 말할 때 써요. 같은 뜻으로 '닦아지다'도 써요. 사람이 닦았다고 말할 때는 '닦아 놨어요'가 자연스러워요.
explain_en: This is the passive of '닦다' and focuses on the thing being wiped and its state rather than the person. '닦아지다' is used with a similar meaning. When saying a person wiped something, '닦아 놨어요' sounds more natural.

examples.en: If you eat a lot of sweets, your teeth rot.
I prefer salty snacks to sweet ones.
Lately I keep craving sweet things.
The doctor told me to cut down on sweets.
When I'm stressed, I end up reaching for sweets first.

examples.ko: 저는 단것에 약해서 케이크를 보면 못 참아요.
examples.en: I have a weakness for sweets, so I can't resist cake.

explain: 과자, 사탕, 케이크처럼 단 음식을 두루 가리키는 말이고, 한 단어라서 붙여 써요. '단것이 당기다'처럼 말하고, 소리 나는 대로는 [단걷]이에요. 반대로 짠 음식은 '짠 것'이라고 띄어 써요.
explain_en: It covers sweet foods in general, such as cookies, candy and cake, and is written as one word. A common phrase is '단것이 당기다' (to crave sweets), and it sounds like [단걷]. For salty food you say '짠 것' with a space.

examples.ko: 새 단어는 단어장에 적어 두고 외워요.
examples.en: I write new words in my vocabulary notebook and memorize them.
I carry my vocabulary notebook in my bag.

examples.ko: 단어장이 거의 다 차서 새로 샀어요.
examples.en: My vocabulary notebook was almost full, so I bought a new one.
This vocabulary list is organized by topic.
My friend's vocabulary notebook is organized really neatly.
I also have a word list I made on a phone app.

explain: 직접 단어를 적는 공책도, 단어를 모아 놓은 책이나 앱 목록도 단어장이라고 해요. '단어장을 만들다', '단어장에 적다'처럼 같이 써요.
explain_en: A handwritten notebook of words, or a printed or app-based word list, can all be called 단어장. It goes with '단어장을 만들다' (make one) and '단어장에 적다' (write in one).

examples.en: Maple leaves turn red in autumn.
I picked up the colored leaves that had fallen on the road.
I pressed a colored leaf between the pages of a book to dry it.
I received maple-leaf-shaped cookies as a gift.
When the wind blew, the colored leaves fell in a shower.
The child made a picture out of colored leaves.

explain: '단풍'은 가을에 색이 변한 잎 전체를 말하고, '단풍잎'은 잎 한 장 한 장을 가리켜요. 나무가 물드는 건 '단풍이 들다'라고 하고, '단풍 구경'을 가요. 발음은 [단풍닙]이에요.
explain_en: '단풍' refers to the autumn colors as a whole, while '단풍잎' points to the individual leaves. The color change is '단풍이 들다', and people go on '단풍 구경' trips. The pronunciation is [단풍닙].

examples.en: My child says he wants to go to the moon.
There's a story that rabbits live on the moon.
What would it be like to travel to the moon by spaceship?
I read a story about the moon world in a picture book.

examples.ko: 어릴 때는 달나라가 정말 있는 줄 알았어요.
examples.en: When I was little, I thought a moon world really existed.
In the children's song, cassia trees grow in the moon world.

explain: 동화나 동요, 아이들과 하는 이야기에서 달을 하나의 나라처럼 부르는 말이에요. 과학 이야기에서는 그냥 '달'이라고 해요. '달님'과 함께 아이들 말투에서 자주 들려요.
explain_en: It treats the moon like a country, and is used in fairy tales, children's songs and talk with kids. In scientific contexts people just say '달'. It sounds childlike, like '달님'.

examples.en: Tonight the moon is big and bright too.
The child made a wish to the moon.
Dear moon, please shine on our house too.
The moon is hidden by clouds, so I can't see it.

examples.ko: 할머니가 달님과 토끼 이야기를 해 주셨어요.
examples.en: Grandma told me the story of the moon and the rabbit.
On the full moon, people look at the moon and make wishes.

explain: '달'에 높임 접미사 '-님'을 붙여서 사람처럼 부르는 말이에요. 동화, 동요, 아이에게 말할 때 쓰고 짝말은 '해님'이에요. 일반 설명에서는 그냥 '달'이라고 해요.
explain_en: This is '달' with the honorific suffix '-님', personifying the moon. It is used in fairy tales, songs and when talking to children, and its partner is '해님' (the sun). In ordinary explanations people just say '달'.

en: year of the rooster; rooster zodiac sign

examples.en: My father was born in the year of the rooster and my mother in the year of the horse.

examples.ko: 저와 제 친구는 둘 다 닭띠예요.
examples.en: My friend and I are both born in the year of the rooster.

examples.ko: 닭띠는 열두 띠 중에서 열 번째예요.
examples.en: The rooster is the tenth of the twelve zodiac animals.
What's your zodiac animal? I'm a rooster.
People born in the year of the rooster formed a group.
I checked what this year's fortune is for the rooster sign.

explain: '띠'는 태어난 해를 상징하는 동물이고, 닭띠, 소띠처럼 동물 이름 뒤에 붙여요. 같은 띠는 열두 해마다 돌아와요. 처음 만난 사람에게 '무슨 띠예요?'라고 물어 나이를 짐작하기도 해요.
explain_en: '띠' is the zodiac animal of the year you were born, attached after the animal name, as in 닭띠 or 소띠. The same sign comes back every twelve years. People sometimes ask '무슨 띠예요?' to guess someone's age.

examples.en: My father works as a professor at a university in the provinces.
To become a university professor, you need a doctorate.
When I was young, I dreamed of becoming a professor.
He is a famous professor, so he gives many lectures.
I sent my question to the professor by email.
The professor's office is on the fourth floor.

explain: 직업을 말할 때는 '대학교수'를 쓰고, 직접 부를 때는 '교수님'이라고 해요. 이름 뒤에도 '김 교수님'처럼 '교수님'을 붙여요. '선생님'보다 '교수님'이 대학에서는 더 정확한 호칭이에요.
explain_en: Use '대학교수' to name the job, but when addressing the person, say '교수님'. After a surname you attach '교수님' too, as in '김 교수님'. At a university, '교수님' is the more accurate title than '선생님'.

examples.en: Washing my hands in warm water warms me up.
I drink a glass of warm water every morning.
No hot water comes out of the tap.
Soaking my feet in warm water relieved my fatigue.
Please mix hot and cold water half and half.
On cold days, a hot shower is the best.

explain: 반대말은 '찬물'이에요. 말할 때는 '뜨거운 물'이나 '따뜻한 물'을 더 자주 쓰고, 안내문이나 설명서에서는 '온수'를 많이 봐요. '더운물'은 샤워, 세수처럼 씻을 때 자연스럽게 나와요.
explain_en: The opposite is '찬물' (cold water). In speech people often say '뜨거운 물' or '따뜻한 물', and signs or manuals often use '온수'. '더운물' comes up naturally when washing, such as showering or washing your face.

examples.en: My child has started learning addition.
We learn addition and subtraction at school.
Addition is easy, but multiplication is hard.
Many children add on their fingers.
The answer to this addition problem is wrong.

examples.ko: 덧셈 문제를 다 풀면 놀러 가도 돼요.
examples.en: Once you finish the addition problems, you can go out to play.

explain: 짝말은 '뺄셈'이고, 곱셈, 나눗셈과 함께 사칙연산이에요. 식을 소리 내어 읽을 때는 '삼 더하기 사는 칠'처럼 '더하기'를 써요. '덧셈'은 사이시옷 때문에 [덛쎔]으로 소리 나요.
explain_en: Its counterpart is '뺄셈', and with 곱셈 and 나눗셈 it makes the four operations. When reading an equation aloud you say '삼 더하기 사는 칠' with '더하기'. Because of the 사이시옷, it sounds like [덛쎔].

examples.en: At lunchtime I read books in the library room.
The library room is quiet, so it's good for studying.
I went to the library room and borrowed a book.

examples.ko: 우리 학교 도서실은 네 시에 문을 닫아요.
examples.en: Our school's library room closes at four o'clock.
You must not make noise in the library room.
I agreed to meet my friend in front of the library room.

explain: '도서관'이 독립된 건물이나 큰 공공 시설을 말할 때가 많다면, '도서실'은 학교나 회사 안에 있는 작은 방에 더 잘 어울려요. 그래서 학교 이야기에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: '도서관' often means a standalone building or a large public facility, while '도서실' fits a small room inside a school or company. That is why it shows up often in school conversations.

examples.en: My house is southeast of the school.
A lot of sunlight comes in through the southeast window.
The typhoon is moving up from the southeast.
Point to the southeast on the map.

examples.ko: 동남쪽으로 십 분쯤 걸으면 역이 나와요.
examples.en: If you walk southeast for about ten minutes, you'll reach the station.
The sky cleared up first in the southeast.

explain: 동쪽과 남쪽 사이의 방향이에요. '남동쪽'이라고도 말해요. 반대 방향은 '서북쪽'이에요.
explain_en: It is the direction between east and south. People also say '남동쪽'. The opposite direction is '서북쪽'.

examples.en: I put tofu and zucchini in the doenjang soup.
The doenjang soup my mother makes is the most delicious.
I add cabbage and boil doenjang soup.
I kept breakfast simple with doenjang soup.
Could you give me a little more doenjang soup?

examples.ko: 이 된장국은 너무 짜서 물을 더 부었어요.
examples.en: This doenjang soup was too salty, so I added more water.

explain: 된장찌개와 달리 보통 국물이 더 많고 맑게 먹는 국이에요. 된장찌개는 건더기가 많고 더 걸쭉하게 끓이는 경우가 많아요. 배추, 시금치, 두부 같은 재료를 넣어요.
explain_en: Compared with 된장찌개, it is usually a soup with more, lighter broth. 된장찌개 is often thicker and has more ingredients. Typical additions are cabbage, spinach and tofu.

examples.en: There is a persimmon tree in our backyard.
The children play ball in the backyard.
I'm thinking of making a vegetable patch in the backyard.
The startled puppy ran out to the backyard.
I mowed the backyard lawn on the weekend.
Our backyard is quieter than the front yard.

explain: 앞마당의 반대말이에요. 비슷한 말로 '뒤뜰'도 있어요. 마당이 있는 단독주택 이야기에서 자주 나오고 아파트에는 보통 없어요.
explain_en: It is the opposite of '앞마당' (front yard). A similar word is '뒤뜰'. It comes up when talking about houses with a yard, and apartments usually don't have one.

examples.en: The back of my hair was flattened, so I wore a hat.
Check the shape of the back of your hair in the mirror.

examples.ko: 샤워 후라서 뒷머리는 아직 안 말랐어요.
examples.en: I just showered, so the back of my hair isn't dry yet.
At the salon I only had the back of my hair trimmed a little.
Shall I braid the back of your younger sibling's hair nicely?
Someone stuck gum in the back of my hair.

explain: 머리 뒤쪽의 머리카락이에요. 머리 뒷부분 자체는 '뒤통수'예요. 짝이 되는 '앞머리'는 보통 이마를 덮는 짧은 머리를 가리켜요.
explain_en: This is the hair at the back of the head. The back of the head itself is '뒤통수'. The counterpart '앞머리' usually means the short hair over the forehead, like bangs.

examples.en: Please hold the door for the person behind you.
There are people behind you too, so please be quick.

examples.ko: 앞사람이 먼저 하고 뒷사람은 나중에 하세요.
examples.en: The person in front goes first, and the one behind goes later.
I gave up my seat to the person behind me on the subway.

examples.ko: 줄을 설 때 뒷사람과 간격을 두세요.
examples.en: When standing in line, leave some space from the person behind you.
At the movie theater, the person behind me kept kicking my seat.

explain: 짝말은 '앞사람'이고, 줄을 서거나 순서를 기다릴 때 자주 써요. 같은 뜻으로 '뒤에 있는 사람'이라고 풀어서 말하기도 해요. 어느 쪽이든 줄 서기, 극장, 대중교통 같은 상황에서 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: Its counterpart is '앞사람', and it is often used when queuing or waiting for your turn. People also say it in full as '뒤에 있는 사람'. Both fit situations such as lines, theaters and public transport.

examples.en: In a hurry, I put my wallet in my jeans' back pocket.
The phone in my back pocket got pressed against the chair.

examples.ko: 오래 입은 바지 뒷주머니의 단추가 떨어졌어요.
examples.en: The button on the back pocket of my old pants came off.
When I went to do laundry, I found a receipt in the back pocket.
You have to be careful with a back pocket when you sit.
These jeans have big back pockets.

explain: 바지 뒤쪽에 달린 주머니예요. 앞쪽 주머니는 '앞주머니'라고 해요. 청바지 이야기에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is the pocket on the back of trousers. The pocket on the front is '앞주머니'. It comes up often when talking about jeans.

examples.en: I'm tall, so I always sit in the back row.
The sound doesn't carry well to the back row.
Students in the back row, please come to the front.

examples.ko: 사진 찍을 때 키 큰 사람은 뒷줄로 가세요.
examples.en: When taking the photo, tall people please go to the back row.
At the theater, the back-row seats are the most comfortable.
Class is over, so please leave in order starting from the back row.

explain: 반대말은 '앞줄'이에요. 가장 뒤에 있는 줄은 '맨 뒷줄'이라고 해요. 교실, 극장, 단체 사진처럼 사람들이 줄 지어 있는 곳에서 써요.
explain_en: The opposite is '앞줄' (front row). The very last row is called '맨 뒷줄'. It is used where people are arranged in rows, such as classrooms, theaters and group photos.

examples.en: The grandmother from the house behind ours gave us persimmons.
A child my age lives in the house behind ours.
The dog from the house behind ours barked all night.
The house behind ours moved away, so it became quiet.
I took some rice cakes over to the house behind ours.
I greeted the new neighbors who moved into the house behind ours.

explain: 우리 집 뒤에 있는 이웃집이에요. 앞에 있는 집은 '앞집', 바로 옆에 있는 집은 '옆집'이라고 해요. 주로 단독주택이 모인 동네에서 쓰는 말이에요.
explain_en: It is the neighboring house behind yours. The house in front is '앞집' and the one right next door is '옆집'. It is used mostly in neighborhoods of detached houses.

examples.ko: 산에 갈 때는 등산화를 꼭 신어요.
examples.en: I always wear hiking boots when I go up a mountain.

examples.ko: 새로 등산화 한 켤레 사야 해요.
examples.en: I need to buy a new pair of hiking boots.
Tie your hiking boot laces tightly.
It rained and my hiking boots got soaked.
These hiking boots are light and don't slip.
I'll change into my hiking boots and set out.

explain: 산에 오를 때 신는 튼튼한 신발이에요. 신발은 '켤레'로 세고 '신다, 벗다'와 함께 써요. 가볍게 걸을 때 신는 '운동화'와는 구별해서 말해요.
explain_en: These are sturdy shoes worn when climbing mountains. Shoes are counted with '켤레' and used with '신다' (put on) and '벗다' (take off). People distinguish them from '운동화' (sneakers) used for casual walking.

examples.en: I bought a digital camera to take on a trip.

examples.ko: 디지털카메라로 찍으면 바로 확인할 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you shoot with a digital camera, you can check right away.
Nowadays people take photos with their phones more than with digital cameras.
The digital camera battery has run out.
This digital camera is small and light.
About a thousand photos fit on the digital camera.

explain: 줄여서 '디카'라고 많이 말해요. 필름을 쓰는 '필름 카메라'와 구별할 때 써요. 외래어라서 보통 붙여 써요.
explain_en: It is often shortened to '디카'. You use it to distinguish it from a film camera. As a loanword, it is normally written without spaces.

examples.en: This morning I spread strawberry jam on bread and ate it.
I received a jar of strawberry jam as a gift.
We also sell homemade strawberry jam.
Keep the strawberry jam in the refrigerator.
I like grape jam better than strawberry jam.
We've run out of strawberry jam, so I need to go to the supermarket.

explain: 잼은 빵에 '바르다'와 함께 써요. 표준 표기는 '잼'이라서 '쨈'이라고 쓰지 않아요. 병으로 사기 때문에 '한 병'으로 세요.
explain_en: Jam goes with the verb '바르다' (to spread) on bread. The standard spelling is '잼', not '쨈'. It is sold in jars, so you count it as '한 병'.

examples.en: My daughter started elementary school this year.

examples.ko: 우리 딸애는 그림을 정말 잘 그려요.
examples.en: My daughter draws really well.
My daughter has grown a lot too.

examples.ko: 딸애에게 생일 선물을 사 주려고 해요.
examples.en: I'm planning to buy a birthday present for my daughter.
My daughter's friends came over to play.
I'm going to the school to pick up my daughter.

explain: 주로 부모가 자기 딸을 편하게 가리킬 때 써요. 남의 딸을 높여 말할 때는 '따님'이라고 해요. 격식 있는 자리에서는 그냥 '딸'이나 '제 딸'을 쓰기도 해요.
explain_en: Parents mostly use it to refer to their own daughter in a relaxed way. When referring to someone else's daughter respectfully, say '따님'. In formal settings people may simply say '딸' or '제 딸'.

examples.en: The cat jumped lightly up onto the wall.
The children are so excited that they bounce up and down.

examples.ko: 돌고래가 물 위로 높이 뛰어오르는 모습을 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw a dolphin leaping high out of the water.

examples.ko: 저 선수는 정말 높이 뛰어오를 수 있어요.
examples.en: That athlete can jump really high.

examples.ko: 개구리가 갑자기 내 발 위로 뛰어올라서 놀랐어요.
examples.en: A frog suddenly jumped onto my foot and startled me.
I was running up the stairs and fell.

explain: '뛰다'와 '오르다'가 합쳐진 말이라서 위로 힘껏 뛰는 동작이나 달려서 위로 올라가는 동작에 써요. 반대말은 '뛰어내리다'예요. '오르다'가 르 불규칙이라서 '뛰어올라요, 뛰어올랐어요'가 돼요.
explain_en: Combining '뛰다' and '오르다', it describes jumping up energetically or running upward. The opposite is '뛰어내리다'. Because '오르다' is a 르-irregular verb, it becomes '뛰어올라요' and '뛰어올랐어요'.

examples.en: On the weekend I went roller skating in the park.
It was my first time roller skating, so I kept falling.
I bought the protective gear needed for roller skating.
My younger sibling is really good at roller skating.

examples.ko: 롤러스케이트 탈 때는 보호대를 꼭 하세요.
examples.en: Be sure to wear protective gear when roller skating.
As a kid I often went to the roller skating rink.

explain: 스케이트를 탈 때처럼 '롤러스케이트를 타다'라고 하고 '하다'는 쓰지 않아요. 바퀴가 한 줄로 달린 '인라인스케이트'도 있어요. 넘어질 수 있어서 손목, 무릎 보호대를 같이 말하곤 해요.
explain_en: Like other skating, you say '롤러스케이트를 타다', not '하다'. There is also '인라인스케이트', with the wheels in one line. Because you can fall, people often mention wrist and knee guards along with it.

examples.en: My lips were dry, so I put on a little lip gloss.
With lip gloss, your lips look moist.
This lip gloss isn't sticky.
I even have two lip glosses in my bag.

examples.ko: 립글로스 색깔이 너무 진한 것 같아요.
examples.en: The lip gloss color seems too dark.
I made my lips shiny with lip gloss.

explain: 입술에 윤기를 주는 화장품이에요. 색을 진하게 내는 '립스틱'과 달리 반짝이는 느낌을 줄 때 자주 말해요. 입술에 '바르다'와 함께 써요.
explain_en: It is a cosmetic that gives the lips a glossy look. Unlike '립스틱', which is for strong color, it is often mentioned for a shiny finish. It goes with the verb '바르다' (to apply).

examples.en: I'm the youngest son of three brothers.
Our youngest son got into university this time.
The youngest son still acts spoiled.
Grandmother cherishes her youngest son the most.

examples.ko: 동네 어르신이 저를 보고 '자네, 이 집 막내아들 아닌가?' 하고 물으셨어요.
examples.en: A neighborhood elder looked at me and asked, 'Aren't you the youngest son of this house?'
The whole family gathered for the youngest son's wedding.

explain: '막내'만 말해도 되지만 아들임을 밝히고 싶을 때 '막내아들'이라고 해요. 짝말은 '맏아들'이고, 딸이면 '막내딸'이에요. 집안에서 막내는 귀여움을 받는 자리라 '막내아들은 아직도 어리광을 부려요' 같은 말이 자연스러워요.
explain_en: '막내' alone is enough, but you say '막내아들' when you want to make clear it is a son. Its counterpart is '맏아들' (eldest son), and for a daughter it is '막내딸'. The youngest is often the one who gets doted on at home, so a sentence like '막내아들은 아직도 어리광을 부려요' sounds natural.

en: year of the horse; horse zodiac sign

examples.en: I was born in the year of the horse and my younger sibling in the year of the dog.
People born in the year of the horse gathered in one place.
My father is a horse, and my mother is a sheep.

examples.ko: 동갑이라서 알아봤더니 우리는 둘 다 말띠예요.
examples.en: We're the same age, and I found out we're both horses.

examples.ko: 말띠는 열두 띠 중에서 일곱 번째예요.
examples.en: The horse is the seventh of the twelve zodiac animals.
People of the same horse sign formed a group.

explain: '소띠, 개띠'처럼 '동물 이름+띠'로 말해요. 상대의 띠를 높여 물을 때는 '무슨 띠세요?'라고 하고, 대답은 '말띠예요'라고 해요. 같은 띠인지 말하면서 나이를 알게 될 때가 많아요.
explain_en: Like 소띠 and 개띠, it is formed as animal name plus 띠. To ask someone's sign politely, say '무슨 띠세요?', and the answer is '말띠예요'. Talking about whether you share a sign often reveals each other's age.

examples.en: This bus leaves on the hour every hour.

examples.ko: 수업 중에는 매시간 십 분씩 쉬어요.
examples.en: During class we take a ten-minute break every period.
I set the alarm to ring every hour.

examples.ko: 매시간 물을 한 잔씩 마시려고 해요.
examples.en: I'm trying to drink a glass of water every hour.
There is a train to the airport every hour.
We have homework in every class, so it's hard.

explain: '한 시간마다'와 같은 뜻으로 쓰고, 학교에서는 수업 시간마다라는 뜻으로도 써요. 짝말은 '매일, 매주, 매달'이에요. 시간표 이야기에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It means the same as '한 시간마다', and at school it can mean every class period. It goes with '매일, 매주, 매달'. It comes up often when discussing timetables.

examples.en: I wrote my name in big letters on my bag with a marker.
Marker writing doesn't come off easily.
Make sure to keep the marker's cap closed.
The child scribbled on the wall with a marker.
Please lend me just one black marker.
The marker smells a bit.

explain: 글씨가 잘 지워지지 않아서 이름을 쓰거나 큰 글씨를 쓸 때 써요. 같은 종류를 '네임펜'이라고도 해요. '사인펜'은 따로 있는 다른 말이에요.
explain_en: Its writing doesn't come off easily, so it is used for writing names or large letters. The same kind of pen is also called '네임펜'. '사인펜' is a different word for a different kind of pen.

examples.en: I changed into cotton pants instead of jeans.
In summer I wear thin cotton pants.
Cotton pants are fine to wash in the washing machine.
I want to buy a pair of beige cotton pants.

examples.ko: 이 면바지가 몸에 좀 꽉 껴요.
examples.en: These cotton pants are a bit tight on me.
Wearing a shirt with cotton pants looks neat.

explain: 면 소재로 만든 바지라서 청바지와 구별해서 말해요. 바지는 '입다'와 함께 쓰고 '한 벌, 두 벌'로 세요. 단정한 느낌이 필요할 때 많이 말해요.
explain_en: These are trousers made of cotton, so people distinguish them from jeans. Pants go with '입다' (to wear) and are counted as '한 벌, 두 벌'. They are mentioned when you want a neat look.
